small_guidance:
- The inner-loop gather over (kd,kh,kw,ic) recomputes weight loads per spatial window position; hoist the per-(d_o,h_o,w_o) modular-stride check using the equivalent split-by-residue trick: only iterate kd values where (d_o+PAD-kd) % STRIDE == 0 — for stride=2 and KS=5 only 3 of the 5 kd values contribute per d_o parity. Precompute valid (kd,kh,kw) triples per (dd,hh,ww) at compile time via tl.static_range branches based on parity.
- Reduce the 6×6×6=216-point window loop by computing convT into a register tile of shape [POOL,POOL,POOL,BLOCK_OC] once per (n,od,oh,ow) and then reducing — current code recomputes the full convT gather at each of 216 spatial positions. Even partial reuse along the innermost (ww) axis would cut redundant weight loads by ~2×.
- Add autotune configs with num_warps=2 (BLOCK_OC=64 is small enough that 4 warps may be underutilized given the heavy register pressure) and try splitting BLOCK_OC=32 with two programs along OC tile to free registers.
large_guidance:
- Restructure as scatter-add ConvTranspose: one program per (n, ic-tile, d_i, h_i, w_i) input voxel, scatter `input * weight` outer-product into a privately-held output tile in shared memory / registers for one (n, od_tile, oh_tile, ow_tile) pool-output region. After the scatter, apply the 6×6×6 max-reduce and OC sum in-kernel. This eliminates the 216× redundant weight gather of the current per-output-point approach.
- Alternative: split into two persistent kernels — (1) a properly tiled im2col GEMM scatter-add ConvT writing the (N,OC,63,63,63) tensor in channels-last layout, (2) a fused max-pool6 + channel-sum kernel. The current monolithic kernel does O(POOL³·KS³·IC·OC) work per output point (≈216·125·32·64 ≈ 55M MACs per output scalar) — completely arithmetic-bound on redundant reloads.
- Use channels_last (NDHWC) for the convT intermediate so the OC=64 axis is contiguous; this lets the pool+sum kernel coalesce the 64-wide channel vector and do the max-then-sum in one register reduction per output voxel.
